:::{#exm-noise-mean-zero}
#### A new outcome that is 4 or 6 with equal probability

Suppose a new outcome at $\predvar$ is $4$ or $6$, each with [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) $1/2$.
Its [population mean](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-expectation) is $\truemeanf{\predvar} = 5$,
so its [noise](#def-noise) is $-1$ or $+1$, each with probability $1/2$.
The population mean of the noise is $\paren{-1} \cdot \frac{1}{2} + 1 \cdot \frac{1}{2} = 0$, as @thm-noise-mean-zero says.

:::
